request: five numbers have a mean of 6; four of them are 4, 7, 5 and 9: what is the fifth?

beats.intent: Four bars of heights 4, 7, 5 and 9, and an empty fifth bar with a question mark
beats.narration: Five numbers have a mean of six. We know four of them: four, seven, five and nine.
beats.code:
stage.title("The missing number")
ax = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 10, 2], x_length=5.5, y_length=4, axis_config={"include_numbers": True}, tips=False).move_to([-3.2, -0.6, 0])
stage.play(Create(ax))
stage.add(ax)
vals = [4, 7, 5, 9]
bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.6, height=ax.c2p(0, v)[1] - ax.c2p(0, 0)[1], color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6).move_to(ax.c2p(i + 1, v / 2)) for i, v in enumerate(vals)])
gap = DashedVMobject(Rectangle(width=0.6, height=1.0, color=GREY_B), num_dashes=16).move_to(ax.c2p(5, 1.2))
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromEdge(b, DOWN) for b in bars], lag_ratio=0.2), Create(gap))
stage.add(bars, gap)
qm = Text("?", font_size=36, color=YELLOW).move_to(gap)
stage.play(FadeIn(qm))

beats.intent: A dashed line at height 6 across all five bars: the mean
beats.narration: A mean of six means that if the five were levelled out, each would be six. So together they must total five times six: thirty.
beats.code:
mean = DashedLine(ax.c2p(0.4, 6), ax.c2p(5.6, 6), color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(mean))
stage.add(mean)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("mean 6\ntotal 30", font_size=24, color=GREEN).move_to(ax.c2p(6.6, 6))))

beats.intent: The four known bars adding to 25, leaving 5 for the last
beats.narration: The four we know add to twenty five. That leaves five for the missing number.
beats.code:
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("4 + 7 + 5 + 9 = 25", font_size=26, color=BLUE).move_to(ax.c2p(2.5, 10.8))))
last = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=ax.c2p(0, 5)[1] - ax.c2p(0, 0)[1], color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.7).move_to(ax.c2p(5, 2.5))
stage.play(FadeOut(gap), FadeOut(qm), GrowFromEdge(last, DOWN))
stage.add(last)
stage.label(last, "5", direction=UP, color=ORANGE)

beats.narration: Total equals mean times count: thirty, minus the twenty five we have, is five.

request: how can you find the volume of a stone by dropping it in water?

beats.intent: A measuring jug of water at 200 ml and a stone beside it
beats.narration: A stone is too lumpy to measure with a ruler. Put two hundred millilitres of water in a measuring jug.
beats.code:
stage.title("Volume by displacement")
k = 0.8
base = -2.4
jug = Rectangle(width=1.8, height=4.3, color=WHITE).move_to([-4.0, base + 2.15, 0])
ticks = VGroup(*[Line([-3.1, base + m * k, 0], [-3.45, base + m * k, 0], color=WHITE) for m in range(6)])
nums = VGroup(*[Text(str(100 * m), font_size=22).move_to([-2.55, base + m * k, 0]) for m in range(6)])
water = Rectangle(width=1.7, height=2 * k, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0).move_to([-4.0, base + k, 0])
stone = Polygon([-1.6, -1.6, 0], [-1.0, -1.4, 0], [-0.7, -1.9, 0], [-1.1, -2.3, 0], [-1.7, -2.1, 0], color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.9)
stage.play(Create(jug), Create(ticks), FadeIn(nums), FadeIn(water), FadeIn(stone))
stage.add(jug, ticks, nums, water, stone)
l200 = stage.label(water, "200 ml", direction=LEFT, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: The stone sinking into the jug and the water level rising to 260 ml
beats.narration: Drop the stone in. It pushes water out of its way, and the level rises to two hundred and sixty.
beats.code:
stage.play(FadeOut(l200))
stage.play(stone.animate.scale(0.8).move_to([-4.0, base + 0.4, 0]), water.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(2.6 * k).move_to([-4.0, base + 1.3 * k, 0]), run_time=1.5)
stage.add(stone, water)
lvl = Arrow([-5.6, base + 2.6 * k, 0], [-4.95, base + 2.6 * k, 0], buff=0, color=GREEN)
stage.play(GrowArrow(lvl))
stage.add(lvl)
stage.label(lvl, "260 ml", direction=LEFT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The 60 ml rise highlighted as the stone's volume
beats.narration: The rise is exactly the space the stone takes up: sixty millilitres.
beats.code:
rise = Rectangle(width=1.7, height=0.6 * k, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0).move_to([-4.0, base + 2.3 * k, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(rise))
stage.add(rise)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("rise = stone", font_size=26, color=YELLOW).move_to([-0.9, base + 2.3 * k, 0])))

beats.narration: Sixty millilitres is sixty cubic centimetres: the volume of the stone.

request: how do you find the volume of a triangular prism?

beats.intent: A triangular prism: a triangle 4 wide and 3 tall stretched 10 long
beats.narration: A tent shape: a triangle four wide and three tall at each end, ten long.
beats.code:
stage.title("Volume of a prism")
k = 0.5
o = np.array([-5.6, -1.8, 0])
q = 10 * k * 0.45 * np.array([1, 0.5, 0])
f = [o, o + 4 * k * RIGHT, o + np.array([2 * k, 3 * k, 0])]
front = Polygon(*f, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5)
back = Polygon(*[p + q for p in f], color=ORANGE, stroke_opacity=0.6)
edges = VGroup(*[Line(p, p + q, color=WHITE) for p in f])
stage.play(Create(back), Create(edges), Create(front))
stage.add(back, edges, front)
stage.label(Line(f[0], f[1]), "4", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(Line(f[1], f[1] + q), "10", direction=DR)

beats.intent: The triangle's height 3 drawn and its area 6 marked
beats.narration: The end triangle has area half of four times three: six square units.
beats.code:
h = DashedLine(o + 2 * k * RIGHT, f[2], color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(h))
stage.add(h)
stage.label(h, "3", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(front.animate.set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.6))
stage.label(front, "area 6", direction=LEFT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Copies of the triangle sliding back along the prism like slices
beats.narration: The prism is that same triangle all the way along: ten units of slices of area six.
beats.code:
slices = VGroup(*[front.copy().set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.15).set_stroke(YELLOW, 1).shift(q * t / 5) for t in range(1, 6)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(sl) for sl in slices], lag_ratio=0.2))
stage.add(slices)

beats.narration: Volume of a prism is the area of its end times its length: six times ten, sixty cubic units.
